title: Sieve daemon: AGPL isolation + header fallback
description:
Isolate the AGPL sieve-rs dependency into a standalone daemon process so usenet-ipfs-smtp becomes MIT-licensed.

Why this issue exists:
usenet-ipfs-smtp is currently AGPL because it links usenet-ipfs-sieve which links sieve-rs (AGPL-3.0-only). Moving sieve evaluation into a separate binary breaks the link; smtp becomes MIT. The daemon communicates over a Unix socket using plain HTTP. When the daemon is unreachable the smtp pipeline falls back to header-based newsgroup routing.

What needs to be done:
- New usenet-ipfs-sieve-daemon binary (AGPL): Axum server on Unix socket, stateless sieve evaluator with compiled-script cache, /health + /check + /filter endpoints
- smtp sieve_client: hyper-over-Unix-socket client calling daemon; fallback_routing() parsing Newsgroups / List-ID / X-List-ID / X-Listid / X-List-Id headers when daemon unreachable
- Wire into session.rs and sieve_admin.rs; drop usenet-ipfs-sieve dep from smtp; change smtp license to MIT
